prompt:
I need the front end for Pairwise Club. Free tournament-running software for volunteer-run chess clubs that pairs Swiss-system events and walks first-time volunteer tournament directors through each rule decision as it comes up.

Who's using it: Hannah Oduya, a parent volunteer at a nonprofit youth chess club that meets in a church hall on Saturdays. She plays casually and has never run a tournament. The usual tournament director is away, so she is running the club's monthly rated-practice Swiss today with a borrowed laptop and a two-page handout.

What they're doing right now: Round 2 of 5 has just finished and all the results are in. Before she can pair round 3 she has three problems she doesn't know how to handle: a late arrival wants to join now, a player has gone home sick and needs to be withdrawn, and that leaves an odd number of players, so someone gets a bye, and she doesn't know who should get it or whether it counts as a point. One board's result was also written down as a draw but the kids say it was a win for black. She needs to understand what the software will do and why, fix the result, deal with the late entry and the withdrawal, and post round 3 pairings within about ten minutes, without the parents waiting in the hall seeing her get anything wrong. This is her first time in the software's tournament-running part. She skipped the introduction at setup and is now running into questions mid-event.

What's in the system at this point: Event: 'November Junior Swiss', 5 rounds, G/25+5, club-rated, 34 registered players (ratings 410–1620, sections not split), round 2 complete with 17 results. Late entry: Theo Brandt, age 9, rating 780, arrived 11:20. Withdrawal: Priya Nand, 1-1 after two rounds. Disputed board: board 6, Okafor vs. Lindqvist, recorded ½-½, players report 0-1. Club settings: half-point byes allowed for late entries in rounds 1–2 only, full-point bye goes to the lowest-rated player in the lowest score group who hasn't had one, colour-balance rules on, tiebreaks Buchholz Cut-1 then Sonneborn-Berger. Standings after round 2: 8 players on 2, 16 on 1 or 1½, 10 on 0 or ½. The club's rules note, written by the regular director (M. Feld), and a glossary of 12 terms (bye, score group, colour due, float, etc.).

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
